units: <cite ref="Mishnah Middot 2:1">Midd. II, 1</cite>, a. fr. <he>הַר הבית</he> the Temple mount.

<cite ref="Yevamot 17a:7">Yeb. 17ᵃ</cite> (play on <he>ה̇ר̇פ̇נ̇יא</he>) <he>ה̇ר̇ שהכל פ̇ונ̇ין בו</he> a hill to which all turn (whose spurious descent prevents them from getting wives elsewhere); a. v. fr.—
<cite ref="Chullin 39b:19">Ḥull. 39ᵇ</cite> (in Chald. diction) <he>רישיך והר</he> here is thy head and here the mountain (a colloquial phrase for compelling one to give up a bargain).—
Ex. R. s. 28 (ref. to Ex. XIX, 3) בזכות הה׳ for the merit of the distinguished one (Abraham), ואין הה׳ אלא אבות har means the patriarchs (ref. to Mic. VI, 2).

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 107a:2">Snh. 107ᵃ</cite> <he>ה׳ שבכם</he> the most prominent of you; a. fr.—[For proper nouns composed with <cite ref="E00808"><he>הר</he></cite>, v. respective determinants.]—Pl. <cite ref="T00374"><he>הָרִים</he></cite>, <cite ref="E00904"><he>הֲרָרִים</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Tamid 32a:72">Tam. 32ᵃ</cite>, a. e. <he>הָרֵי חושך</he>, v. <cite ref="H00490"><he>חו̇שֶׁךְ</he></cite>.—
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 24a:8">Snh. 24ᵃ</cite> <he>עוקר הרי הרים</he> uprooting the highest mountains (a figure for dialectical ingenuity).
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 1:6:4">Y. Yeb. I, 3ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>בין שני הֶהָ׳ וכ׳</he> between the two high mountains (great scholars).
<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 15:1">Ex. R. s. 15</cite> <he>ואין ה׳ אלא אבות</he>, v. supra.—
<cite ref="Mishnah Chagigah 1:8">Ḥag. I, 8</cite> <he>כה׳ תלויין בשערה</he> like mountains suspended on a hair (a slender Bible text for numerous Talmudic laws); a. v. fr.
